# Background

In a mouse model of colitis, a blocking antibody against IL-23 reduces disease. Two explanations are
still open: IL-23 acts on RORgt+ CD4 T cells, or IL-23 acts on group 3 innate lymphoid cells
(ILC3s). Reported so far: both populations express IL-23R; the blocking antibody reduces disease in
Rag1-KO mice, which have ILC3s but no T cells; the antibody also reduces disease in wild-type mice;
and untreated Rag1-KO mice reach about half the disease score of untreated wild-type mice. A
conditional Il23r allele, a Cd4-Cre line and a Rorc-Cre line are all available.

# Question

Which experiment would decide between the two explanations?

# Answer format

Reply with exactly one JSON object in this schema; it is saved verbatim to /app/output/answer.json and graded, including the rationale (at most 400 words; text beyond the cap is ignored).

```json
{
  "answer": {
    "experiment": "<the experiment, in a few sentences>"
  },
  "rationale": "<your derivation>"
}
```
